scores.evidence: Commits are created with the Git Data API (blob → tree → commit → ref) on `issue-agent/<issue>-<slug>`.
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (HMAC, delivery-id dedup, SKIP LOCKED, App permissions, workflows permission, fork PR secrets rules) are accurate; minor issues like Fargate egress-control via security groups and Object Lock claims are plausible but slightly loose.

scores.evidence: Milestone 1 tests an off-the-shelf coding agent ... If it's as good, we keep our own triage and policy layer and drop the custom fix loop.
scores.rationale: Covers triage and resolve, resolves ambiguities with explicit defaults, and gives explicit non-goals and go/no-go deferrals.

scores.evidence: Neither worker writes to GitHub. They send proposed actions to the Policy Engine ... Approved actions go to the GitHub Gateway, the only code that holds write credentials
scores.rationale: Data ownership, trust zones and idempotency are consistently applied across components, flows and decisions with import-linter enforcement.

scores.evidence: Shadow precision ≥ 85% on ≥ 100 live issues before going live; ... Injection: Adversarial suite ... blocks at < 100%
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, riskiest assumptions are spiked early, and continues in production via sampling and weekly regression; thresholds are labelled as assumptions.

scores.evidence: all targets are assumptions until the pilot teams confirm them
scores.rationale: Assumption table states impact if wrong and how validated, with defaults and owners for open questions.

scores.evidence: The worker crashes after the commit and ref are created but before the PR exists. The lease expires and another worker reclaims the job.
scores.rationale: Covers duplicates, partial failures, injection including via CI, provider outage, env failures and loops with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: Alerts linked to symptoms, each with a runbook: Oldest queued job > 30 min ... Any `blocked` policy violation.
scores.rationale: Monitoring, rollback, runbooks, ownership and migrations are covered and sized to the team; business-hours-only support and a few thin spots (deployment pipeline specifics) keep it from 4.

scores.evidence: Estimated monthly cost at pilot scale: model $150–600 (A10), Fargate sandboxes about $20–50 ... Total roughly $350–950.
scores.rationale: Drivers, ranges with basis, per-run and monthly caps and a buy-vs-build comparison are covered; scaling with usage is somewhat thin.

scores.evidence: | D5 | Control loop runs in the trusted service ... | Hard (trust model) | — |
scores.rationale: Reversibility is tabulated per decision, hard ones (identity, trust model, language) flagged and validated early, with interfaces isolating inner loop, model and sandbox.

scores.evidence: D6 | Postgres for both queue and state ... One technology to run. Load is under 1 job per second
scores.rationale: Mostly simple single service with Postgres queue, but a lot of ceremony (OTel traces, import-linter, Object Lock, Terraform, four milestones) for a 2-3 person pilot.

scores.evidence: T12 ... Test in dev: tools work; `curl https://api.github.com` and the metadata endpoint fail during the agent phase
scores.rationale: Waves of tasks with locations, done-when checks, time-boxed spikes, go/no-go thresholds and adaptation rules make it immediately startable.

checklist.evidence: Non-goals (v1): auto-merging; auto-closing issues; ... D3 | Maintainers trigger fixes; never automatic in v1 ... Pilot PR merge rate ≥ 40%
No `workflows` permission, so GitHub itself refuses changes to workflow files. No Actions, Secrets or Administration permissions.
Flow 4 ... Policy Engine denies it on protected paths; Fixed rules only. No model involved.
There is **no outbound access**: no GitHub, no model API, no instance metadata endpoint. No IAM task role permissions.
the orchestrator itself runs the repo's configured `test` command in the sandbox ... It does not trust the model's claim that tests pass.
Shadow precision ≥ 85% on ≥ 100 live issues before going live; ≥ 150 triage cases
`label_feedback` ... 10% of runs plus every PR that gets rejected or heavily edited are reviewed weekly
60 tool calls; $5 model spend; 25 min wall-clock; abort if the same tool call ... repeats 3 times; Global kill switch (CLI, takes effect within seconds)
A run-level budget is passed in, and the call is refused if it would exceed it. p95 cost ≤ $5 per fix attempt
Audit: the `github_actions` table plus S3 transcripts. S3 Object Lock in governance mode
`search(regex, glob)` ... a repo's similar-issue context comes from GitHub search, not an index.
The unique `delivery_id` makes the second delivery do nothing ... job idempotency key (`repo#issue#label_event_id`)

traps.evidence: A human reviews and merges every change. The agent never merges.
The sandbox never sees a token.
Issue text is input from strangers.
≥ 30% of agent PRs merged with at most light edits.
60 tool calls; $5 model spend; 25 min wall-clock

note: Exceptionally thorough, safety-first plan with trusted-loop/untrusted-sandbox split, measurement gates and buy-vs-build; minor over-engineering and thin triage-side retrieval are the main gaps.
